articles.title: Short stature-related factors and nomogram-based risk prediction in children aged 7-12: evidence from Chaozhou, China.
articles.abstract: Childhood height development is a crucial indicator of public health. A cross-sectional survey of 7,799 children aged 7-12 in Chaozhou City, China. The overall prevalence of short stature was 3.7%. Independent risk factors included short parental height, low birth weight, preterm birth, low exercise, short sleep, and irregular diet. The nomogram model had an AUC of 0.858.

articles.title: Novel RAD50 variants lead to Nijmegen Breakage Syndrome-like disorder and unplanned recombinant human growth hormone treatment response.
articles.abstract: RAD50 gene mutations cause Nijmegen Breakage Syndrome-like disease, characterized by severe growth retardation and microcephaly. A boy with microcephaly and severe growth restriction received rhGH for 5 years 9 months before genetic analysis identified two novel RAD50 variants. rhGH improved growth (-3.35 to -1.28 SD). This report expands the clinical and genetic scope of RAD50 mutations and raises awareness of the risk-benefit balance of rhGH for syndromic short stature.

articles.title: Epidemiological Trends and Seasonal Patterns in Childhood Type 1 Diabetes: Insights From 2001 to 2024 in Lithuania.
articles.abstract: Type 1 diabetes (T1D) incidence is rising globally. This study examines 24-year trends in childhood T1D incidence and seasonal patterns in Lithuania (2369 patients). The mean IR was 21.4 per 100,000 <15 years; incidence rose from 10.8 to 36.4, with peaks in 2021-2022 aligning with COVID-19 waves. Most new cases (63.5%) were diagnosed September to March.

articles.title: Diagnostic Utility of Genetic Testing in Hyperthyroxinemia With Non-Suppressed TSH.
articles.abstract: Hyperthyroxinemia with non-suppressed TSH is a complex diagnostic entity. 25 children from 19 families with elevated FT4 and non-suppressed TSH were evaluated. THRB sequencing identified RTHbeta in 33.3% tested; ALB sequencing revealed FDH (hotspot c.725G>A, p.Arg242His) in 46.2% tested. Hotspot analysis of the ALB gene is recommended as a first-line test, particularly in asymptomatic individuals.

Clinical picture of early infancy PTH resistance syndromes: is it time to improve diagnostic criteria?
articles.abstract: Clinical presentation of inactivating PTH/PTHrP signaling disorders (iPPSDs, historically pseudohypoparathyroidism) exhibits pronounced age-dependence. 117 patients followed at two European tertiary centres; median age at diagnosis 5.9 years. Before age 2, minor criteria were more represented than major criteria. The combination of early onset obesity and elevated TSH should trigger genetic screening before 2 years of age.

articles.title: A Phase II Basket Trial of Vosoritide in Children with RASopathies, ACAN and NPR2 Deficiency.
articles.abstract: Vosoritide, a CNP analog, was tested in 30 pre-pubertal children with RASopathy, ACAN or NPR2 deficiency. Annualized growth velocity increased from 4.53 to 8.09 cm/yr (p<0.0001). Vosoritide could be an effective precision medicine for growth disorders affecting the MAPK pathway.

articles.title: Sex- and Pubertal Stage-Specific Bone Microarchitecture and Strength in Adolescents With Type 1 Diabetes.
articles.abstract: Forty youth with T1D and 40 matched controls. Boys with T1D had lower trabecular bone volume fraction and failure load; early-pubertal girls showed no deficits. Mid-puberty in boys represents a critical window for skeletal vulnerability.

articles.title: Clinical characteristics and individualized treatment strategies for children with type 1 diabetes and exogenous insulin antibody syndrome: a retrospective case series and literature review.
articles.abstract: Retrospective case series of five pediatric T1DM+EIAS patients. EIAS is a rare cause of severe glycemic dysregulation. CGM metrics are essential; for refractory cases, mycophenolate mofetil may offer a therapeutic option.

articles.title: Effect of pericentric inversion of chromosome 9 on reproductive outcomes in assisted reproductive technology: a propensity score-matched cohort study.
articles.abstract: Retrospective cohort of 40,502 ART cycles. Pericentric inversion of chromosome 9 was not associated with adverse embryologic or reproductive outcomes, supporting its classification as a benign variant.

articles.title: Case Report: Familial hCG syndrome with elevated hCG level concurrently in blood and cerebrospinal fluid.
articles.abstract: An 8-year-9-month-old girl with central precocious puberty and unexplained hCG elevation in serum and CSF. Familial hCG syndrome was diagnosed after segregation analysis. Expands the phenotypic spectrum of this benign condition.

articles.title: SWIIM study protocol: a pre-post study evaluating the implementation of an established pediatric diabetes management program to improve glycemic outcomes for children and young people with type 1 diabetes.
articles.abstract: Protocol evaluating implementation of the Success with Individualized Insulin Management (SWIIM) program across NSW, Australia. Pre-post-implementation study in three hospitals. SWIIM could provide a scalable model of care for pediatric T1D.

articles.title: Childhood systemic glucocorticoid exposure and subsequent alterations in myocardial structure and cardiac function: a narrative review of clinical evidence.
articles.abstract: Narrative review of childhood systemic glucocorticoid exposure and cardiac outcomes. Most consistent signal is reversible myocardial hypertrophy in neonates/young infants. Evidence supports transient remodeling and risk-factor clustering more than irreversible cardiomyopathy.

articles.title: Systematic or targeted molecular screening of SHOX gene variations in children with idiopathic short stature?
articles.abstract: Retrospective study of 266 ISS patients who underwent SHOX gene analysis. MLPA identified variations in 9.8%; sequencing detected an additional 6%. Systematic molecular screening by MLPA and sequencing is recommended to detect all SHOX gene variants in children with ISS.
